what_this_is: Trillion's own behaviors in a person's account as Workshop tools: each runs inside that person's store (placement:this-account, whose executor looks the row's invoke.action up in the store's own map), so Trillion's defaults (records/starting-rules.json) and the person's own rules, schedules and AIs run them the same way. The placement is included in every plan: these do what Trillion did by itself before they were tools. A row's `retry` ({ max_attempts, first_after_seconds, factor, longest_after_seconds }) says running it again is safe, so a run of it a rule started that fails is started again by itself (src/automations.mjs).

payload.label: Read the service's own watch
payload.job: Read what Trillion's own watch saw last: whether every store answered its calls in the last ten minutes, and whether what landed on main went live within the hour
payload.description: With {}, read the latest saved service-watch snapshot: { said, read_at, watches: { <watch>: { failing, said, evidence, since, last_worked } } }. With build_commit (exactly 40 hexadecimal characters), read just that retained build record from the same service owner, without enumerating keys or running a build. Returns said, read_at, watches: {}, build_commit, build_status (found, absent or unreadable), build, and build_read coverage with explicit byte limits and omissions. KV is eventually consistent; absence does not prove a build never ran. The record's outcome and diagnostics do not by themselves prove the live deployment. Screenshot bytes are not returned. Existing scheduled checks continue to use {}.

build_commit.description: Read this exact retained build's metadata and bounded diagnostics; omit to read the ordinary service-watch snapshot.

build_read.description: The one-key read's retention, eventual consistency, byte limits and explicit omissions. This is not independent proof of deployment.

Everyone who connects that service by signing in then uses this app. remove lists names to take out. With neither, it only says which names are held (true or false, never a value). payload.label: Check everything still works

payload.job: Instead of telling the person what to do, open the exact thing that needs them (a drafted post to approve, stuck work, a decision to answer) as the main pane, start a walkthrough pointing at its own control, and tell them with a link that opens the same on any device

payload.label: Fill a list from a feed
payload.job: Keep one of my lists, or one of the shared libraries, filled from a feed: every item at a web address that answers RSS, Atom or JSON becomes a row or an entry, with its pictures and videos kept in my files
payload.description: Takes list_id, feed (an https address answering RSS, Atom or JSON), items (where the items are in JSON, $.rows when left out; an RSS or Atom feed is read into rows with id, title, link, published and summary), key (each item's identity, $.id when left out), values ({ field id: selector }, which item field fills which list field) and files_into (the folder pictures are kept in). Items already in the list are left as they are, so an edit is never overwritten, unless update_existing is true: then the fields the feed fills are rewritten on rows where the feed now says something else. stamp (the id of a list field) is given the time of the run on every row written or confirmed. into ({ dataset: a shared library id }) sends the items to that shared library instead of a list, in batches, each entry with an id from its key, so an entry the feed repeats unchanged writes nothing; it returns the entries added, replaced, refused and not valid, with the reason for each. A picture or video an item names is kept in the person's files and its media field names it. A schedule runs it to keep the list current. Returns the rows added and updated and how many new items wait for the next run.

most.description: How many new items to add this run (20 when left out); the rest wait for the next run

update_existing.description: Rewrite the fields the feed fills on rows already there when the feed now says something else (false when left out: rows are left as they are)

fixed.description: A value for each field that is the same on every row or entry, like the source the items come from or their licence: { "licence": "MIT" }. It is checked against the field like any other value

list_id.description: The list that holds the row

row_id.description: The row that gets the time

field.description: The field of that list that holds the time

stamp_row.description: After a successful read, writes the time of this run into one field of one row of a list, so the row shows when its feed was last read. One row is written per run

key_prefix.description: Text put in front of every item's id, so ids from different feeds never meet: the prefix "parts/ui/" and the item id "accordion" give "parts/ui/accordion"

stamp.description: The id of a list field that is given the time of this run on every row written or confirmed

into.description: Fill a shared library instead of a list: send this and not list_id

payload.label: Watch my sources
payload.job: Watch the places I follow (any site's feed, a YouTube channel, a blog, a changelog, a page) and keep each new item as a row, weighed against what I am pursuing; only what moves a pursuit is handed to my AIs
payload.description: Reads each source marked Yes in the list sources_list_id (signal-sources when left out; made with its fields name, address, feed, kind, watching and the rest when missing) and keeps every item it has not kept before as a row in items_list_id (signals when left out). The first read of a source keeps what it lists as a baseline and brings nothing in; later reads keep what is new, ask your own AI once for all of them whether each moves a pursuit directly or carries an insight from elsewhere for a pursuit or a content format, and hand only those to your AIs. The rest are set aside. A page is watched by whether its words changed; an X account needs a feed address; a YouTube channel is read from its feed or, when YouTube refuses that, its videos page. A source that answers 'not changed' costs nothing. Reads at most 25 sources and weighs at most 20 items a run; the rest wait for the next. Sends nothing outward. Returns read (sources read), kept (rows added), moves ([{ title, link, pursuit }]), set_aside, waiting (new items not yet weighed), problems ([{ name, problem }]) and sources_waiting.

sources_list_id.description: The list of places to watch (signal-sources when left out)

items_list_id.description: The list the items are kept in (signals when left out)

most_per_source.description: How many of a source's newest items to look at each read (10 when left out)

payload.label: Hold every Trillion page on the one thing that needs the person
payload.job: See or change the hold: while something truly needs the person, every Trillion page they open (web, Mac app, menu bar, iPhone) shows only that one thing until it is done or set aside with a reason; choose in advance what turning it off costs, ask it off, or turn it on
payload.description: op read (the default) answers whether the hold is on, the one thing it holds (held.key, held.card), how many set-asides are left today and the stakes. op aside with key (held.key), title and reason sets the held thing aside for a while; the reason must be words, and it is handed to the AIs to do the thing instead or cut it to one small step. op stake with stake (a stake id) and values (the fields it asks for) chooses what turning the hold off costs; a new stake counts only after the one in force has run its delay. op off asks it off: it turns off only after the stake's delay and comes back by itself a day later, and a stake that tells someone or gives money is handed to the AIs to carry out. op on turns it on at once. The hold is on the person, never on an AI: an AI keeps doing all of its own work while a thing is held, up to the one step only the person can do. Every way out of the hold and its counter is DATA in src/escape-chain.json.

provenance.source: trillion-workshop tools/hold-one-thing-until-done/read-data/needs-you-hold.mjs over src/waiting-on-you.json (hold, sections) and src/escape-chain.json

payload.label: Say it out loud
payload.job: Say words out loud to the person in a natural voice (their own cloned voice or a neutral one), made once by one of their own devices and kept in their files so every device of theirs plays it
payload.description: Runs in the person's account and places the speaking on the first of their awake devices that keeps a speech model (src/placement.json job speak, such as tool:say-with-a-voice-model on their Mac), which makes the sound in the voice of the place it is said in (the person's own list rows, tool:voice-for), else their chosen voice, and keeps it in their files under /Voice/Said at its natural pace. Answers { file, name, seconds, voice, engine, produced_by, made_on, speed }: whoever plays it plays it at `speed` with the pitch kept. Trillion never pays for a voice. With no capable device awake, or when generation fails, it answers { file: null, system_voice: false, retryable: true, text, speed, said }; no sound was made. Keep the request and retry on a capable device. Never substitute a system voice.

voice.description: A voice id of the person's (a row of their Voices list, tool:voice-for); the place's voice, else their chosen voice, when left out

place.description: Where this is said: a row id of the person's list of places Trillion speaks (tool:voice-for lists them, such as said-out-loud, calls, voice-messages, podcasts, posts, car, coaching), whose voice and speed it uses

speed.description: How many times faster than natural to play it, with the pitch kept: the place's speed from the person's rows. The sound is kept at its natural pace.

payload.label: Which voice and how fast
payload.job: Say which voice Trillion speaks in at one place (things said out loud, calls, voice messages, podcasts, posts, the car, coaching) and how fast, with every voice and place the person has
payload.description: Runs in the person's account over their own list rows (src/voices.mjs): the list Voices (their own cloned voices and the voices every person has, each with its speed, one marked Chosen) and the list Where Trillion speaks (each place with its voice and, when set, its own speed). Both lists are made the first time anything asks, with a row for each usual place. Answers { place, voice, speed, voices, places, lists, scale }: the place's own voice, else the chosen one, and the place's own speed, else its voice's, else the scale's default; a speed is how many times faster than natural the voice plays, from scale.min to scale.max. To change a voice or a speed, put rows in those lists (put_list_rows with lists.voices or lists.places); the Ambience screen sets the same rows.

place.description: A row id of the list of places Trillion speaks; the chosen voice and its speed when left out

voice.description: A voice row id that wins over the place's voice

payload.label: Choose how Trillion uses a connected account
payload.job: Turn a selectable Trillion capability on or off for one connected account, or reset it to the default
payload.description: Set a Trillion-use choice for one exact connected account. This does not change the permissions granted to the provider. connection_id and connected_at identify the current account incarnation; capability_id must be a user-selectable capability declared by that service. choice is enabled, disabled, or reset (reset restores the default enabled behavior).
